notes: Illinois has one flat rate, 4.95%, on net income (Line 11 = base income Line 9 less exemption allowance Line 10); it applies to every filing status, and no bracket schedule or surtax is printed.

The booklet prints no standard deduction, and federal itemized deductions may not be subtracted (Schedule M Instructions PDF page 1). The only deduction-like amounts are the Line 10 exemption allowance (10a personal, 10b age 65, 10c blind, 10d dependents).

Dependent amount (Line 10d) comes from Schedule IL-E/EITC Step 2 Line 1, which is not among the documents read; its dollar figure is not printed in them, so no dependent_exemption deduction is recorded. Not found in the booklet.

Exemption chart (Instructions PDF page 8): the Single row includes Single, Head of Household, Widowed and Married filing separately. A federal Qualifying Surviving Spouse chooses Widowed (PDF page 6), so that status has the single amount and the 250,000 test.

Income Exceptions cover the whole Line 10 exemption allowance, so the test is recorded on the personal, age 65 and blind entries alike; it would also remove Line 10d. The word printed is 'greater than', so the amount exactly at the threshold keeps the allowance (applies_when over).

The same Income Exceptions wording removes the property tax and K-12 credits (Instructions PDF page 9). Schedule ICR, which holds those credits, is not among the documents read; no credit is recorded.
Line 2 of the return adds back federally tax-exempt interest and dividend income (federal Form 1040 Line 2a), so the base starts from federal AGI plus that amount plus Schedule M additions.

Social Security: Form IL-1040 Line 5 ('Social Security benefits and certain retirement plan income if included in Line 1'), Instructions PDF page 7 Line 5, and Pub 120 PDF page 2 all subtract the federally taxed benefits.

Line 5 has no dollar cap, no age test and no income test in any of the three documents; only the federally taxed portion, not the gross amount, is subtracted (Pub 120 PDF page 2). 'You may include early distributions from qualified plans and IRAs.'

Other states' government pensions: no sentence names another state or a particular paying state, and no document says they are treated differently from Illinois's. The treatment comes from Pub 120's wording, set out in the settlement note on il_government_pension. No reciprocity rule concerns pensions (the agreements with Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan and Wisconsin are about compensation, Instructions PDF page 3), so paying_states is left out.

Schedule M Instructions PDF page 1, 'May I subtract my out-of-state income? No', answers what Schedule M (Line 7) allows. The same list sends retirement income to Line 5: 'income received from Social Security benefits and retirement plans (including Illinois Teacher's Retirement). Eligible retirement income should be subtracted on Form IL-1040, Line 5.' It is not read as a limit on Line 5.

Pub 120's government bullet says 'reported as wages on your U.S. 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 1z'. That line reference does not narrow the kind: Form IL-1040 Line 5 says 'Generally on fed. Forms 1040/1040-SR, Lines 4b, 5b, and 6b', and Pub 120 PDF page 3 lists government retirement among the items that attach federal pages 1 and 2, with a Form 1099-R when Lines 4b, 5b and 6b do not identify the income.

Annuities are not named on Line 5. Federal Line 5b is labelled 'Pensions & annuities' in the Allocation Worksheet (Instructions PDF page 17), and Pub 120 refuses 'income that is not from a qualified employee benefit plan'; so annuity is in covers_unclear on il_qualified_plan.

Retirement payments to retired partners: the documents disagree. Pub 120 PDF page 3 says report them on Schedule M, and Instructions PDF page 7 says they 'should not be included on Line 5'; Schedule M Instructions PDF page 2, Line 14 says 'Do include these amounts on Form IL-1040, Line 5.' No relief entry is written, because no amount rule is printed and no income kind matches.
Railroad sick pay and railroad unemployment compensation are a separate subtraction on Schedule M Line 37 (Schedule M Instructions PDF page 5); not retirement income, not recorded as a relief.
Municipal interest: treatment other, because Illinois's own bonds are not exempt as a class. Only the listed obligations are (Schedule M Lines 34 and 35).

Capital gains: no rate or deduction different from ordinary income is printed, apart from the Line 5 employer-securities subtraction (il_nua_employer_securities) and the Schedule M Line 23 August 1, 1969 valuation limitation (Schedule F, not among the documents read).
Schedule M prints other subtractions and lump limits (college savings and ABLE contributions 10,000; 20,000 joint) that are not retirement items and are not recorded as reliefs.
Indexing: no document says whether any figure is adjusted for inflation. The exemption is printed under 'What's New for 2025?' as the amount 'for tax year 2025', which is not a statement either way.

Settlement 2026-11-07: indexing: A wrote one all_other entry, B wrote all_other and personal_exemption, both not_stated; Instructions PDF page 1 says only 'The personal exemption amount for tax year 2025 is $2,850', nothing about adjustment, so the single all_other entry stands.

Settlement 2026-11-07: government pensions: A said two entries (public_pension; military_pension), B said one covering public_pension, public_pension_other_state and military_pension; Pub 120 PDF page 2 prints one bullet, 'a government retirement and government disability plan, including military plans', so one entry.

Settlement 2026-11-07: public_pension_other_state: A said covers_unclear, B said covers; Pub 120 says it. PDF page 2 allows 'a government retirement and government disability plan, including military plans', with no limit to Illinois, and that bullet's own 'military plans' shows government is not confined to Illinois's; the next bullet says 'a state or local governmental deferred compensation plan', not an Illinois one; and PDF page 3's refusal turns only on 'plans that are not government plans'. Where Illinois means only Illinois it says so (Schedule M Line 34, 'obligations of Illinois state and local governments'). So it is in covers.

Settlement 2026-11-07: employer plans and IRAs: A said one entry, B said two; Pub 120 PDF page 2 prints separate bullets, and the 10-year averaging refusal on PDF page 3 reaches only a qualified retirement plan, so two entries.

Settlement 2026-11-07: 457 plans: A and B held them in the text of the government entry; Pub 120 PDF page 2 prints a separate bullet that also reports on Line 5b, so il_governmental_457 is its own entry.

Settlement 2026-11-07: other Line 5 items: A said one entry (capital_gains, wages, interest), B said separate entries for employer securities and retirement bonds and left out group term life premiums; Pub 120 PDF page 2 prints a bullet for each with its own condition, so three entries, group term life kept from A.

Settlement 2026-11-07: Schedule M Line 22 covers: A said interest, B said interest and dividends; Schedule M Instructions PDF page 3 says 'distributions received from mutual funds' and never says dividends, so covers is interest, the fund share is in cap_rule, and dividends is in covers_unclear.
Settlement 2026-11-07: Schedule M Line 21 military pay: A left it in notes, B wrote a relief; Schedule M Instructions PDF page 3 prints the subtraction with its exclusions, so B's entry is kept.
